scoring_justification: All headline quantities (formation energies, surface energies, cleavage energies) are recomputed from the raw total_energies artifact against paper‑reported values and structural trends; no trusted self‑reported metric is used.

hidden_assets.purpose: Paper‑reported gold values for formation energies (Table 1), surface energies (Table 2), and cleavage energies (Table 3) as well as the required structural relationships.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper's Tables 1‑3 and textual description of trends.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Exact numbers from the paper's tables; structural checks derived from the paper's stated ordering.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own published results, the target of a reproduction task.

outputs.description: Compiled total energies (eV) of bulk binaries, ternaries, and slab models for both compounds. The checker recomputes bulk formation energies, 2D slab formation energies (under AX-rich and BX2-rich conditions), surface energies of triple-layer slabs (ideal and relaxed), and cleavage energies from this artifact, then compares to hidden reference values with tolerances and verifies ordering trends.

output_contract.notes: All derived quantities (formation energies, surface energies, cleavage energies) are computed by the checker from this single artifact; the solving agent does not compute them.

steps.description: Recompute bulk formation energies for CsPbBr3 and MAPbI3 and compare to paper Table 1 values with tolerance ±0.05 eV.
Recompute surface energies for L3 slabs (CsPbBr3 and MAPbI3, ideal and relaxed, AX and BX2 terminations) and compare to paper Table 2 values with tolerance ±0.05 eV.
Recompute cleavage energies for both compounds (ideal and relaxed) and compare to paper Table 3 values with tolerance ±0.05 eV.
Verify structural trends in relaxed 2D formation energies: AX < BX2 for each compound/thickness; CsPbBr3 all > bulk; MAPbI3 MAI‑terminated <= bulk; monotonic decrease with thickness.
Verify structural trends in surface energies: AX < BX2 for ideal and relaxed; MAI‑relaxed ≤ −0.005 eV; relaxation reduces surface energy (ideal > relaxed).
